speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the nature of your rash; does it appear as small, flat-topped bumps or reddish patches, and do they itch intensely when you scratch them? Additionally, have you noticed any specific skin changes like thickening or darkening, particularly in the creases of your palms?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (PCT) with neuropathy. The combination of photosensitive blisters on sun-exposed areas (face/upper body), skin fragility, and peripheral neuropathy in a patient with potential iron overload from livestock exposure or hemochromatosis is classic for PCT. Have you noticed any blisters forming on your fingers or forehead after sun exposure, or any darkening of your urine?
